answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new agent to post a bonded stake that is locked for a long period and slashed if peers flag its work. Because an attacker must lock real capital for every fake identity, creating many agents becomes expensive. Reputation earned from graded outputs then sits in a lantern-like public ledger, while a cipher-based proof of unique hardware or key ownership keeps one operator from quietly spawning an oasis of duplicate peers.
